For an **upper-upscale hotel in the Caribbean or Latin America**, the owner should build the brand shortlist around the property’s format—urban/MICE, lifestyle conversion, traditional resort, or all-inclusive—rather than selecting solely by chain scale. Brand classifications also vary somewhat by country and data provider.

## Recommended brand universe

| Platform | Brands to prioritize | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Marriott Hotels, Westin, Renaissance, Sheraton, Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio** | Large urban hotels, resorts, mixed-use projects and distinctive conversions. Autograph and Tribute are especially relevant when the owner wants to retain the property’s identity. Marriott positions these within its full-service “premium” portfolio. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hilton** | **Hilton Hotels & Resorts, Curio Collection, Canopy by Hilton** | Hilton for conventional full-service hotels and resorts; Curio for independent/lifestyle conversions and destination resorts; Canopy for urban lifestyle projects. Hilton explicitly identifies Curio as upper-upscale, and both Curio and Canopy are expanding in CALA. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/uploads/2024/04/HLT.Q1-CORP-FactSheet-APR2024.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Regency, Hyatt Centric, The Unbound Collection, Destination by Hyatt, JDV by Hyatt** | Hyatt Regency for larger full-service/MICE assets; Centric and JDV for lifestyle hotels; Unbound and Destination for individualistic resorts and conversions. Hyatt classifies Regency, Centric and JDV as upper-upscale, while Unbound and Destination span upper-upscale and luxury. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Accor** | **Pullman, MGallery Collection**; selectively **Swissôtel or Mövenpick** | Pullman for contemporary urban, convention and larger resort properties; MGallery for boutique, heritage and experiential assets. Accor explicitly positions MGallery in upper-upscale and has strong historical operating depth in Latin America. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |
| **IHG Hotels & Resorts** | **Hotel Indigo, Crowne Plaza**; selectively **Kimpton** | Hotel Indigo for locally inspired lifestyle hotels; Crowne Plaza for business/MICE demand; Kimpton when the project can support the upper boundary of upper-upscale or luxury lifestyle positioning. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/kimpton-hotels-restaurants?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts** | **Wyndham Grand, Registry Collection Hotels** | Wyndham Grand for conventional upper-upscale resorts and urban hotels; Registry for independently styled resorts and conversions. Wyndham explicitly classifies both as upper-upscale, with Registry operating as a soft brand. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/upscale-lifestyle-hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Minor Hotels** | **NH Collection, nhow**; selectively **Tivoli** | Particularly relevant for urban Latin American markets and European/Latin American source demand. NH Collection is the principal premium option; nhow suits lifestyle projects; Tivoli may push into luxury. Minor has an established Latin American operating platform. ([minorhotels.com](https://www.minorhotels.com/en/development?utm_source=openai)) |

## Best brands by project type

### 1. Large urban, business or convention hotel

For a 200-plus-room hotel with meaningful meeting space, prioritize:

- Hyatt Regency
- Marriott Hotels
- Hilton Hotels & Resorts
- Westin
- Sheraton
- Renaissance
- Pullman
- Crowne Plaza
- NH Collection

**Best initial RFP group:** Hyatt Regency, Marriott, Hilton, Pullman and NH Collection. Add Westin or Renaissance where wellness or lifestyle differentiation is important.

### 2. Boutique, heritage or conversion property

For an existing independent hotel, historic building or distinctive 80–250-key asset:

- Autograph Collection
- Tribute Portfolio
- Curio Collection
- The Unbound Collection by Hyatt
- JDV by Hyatt
- MGallery Collection
- Hotel Indigo
- Registry Collection Hotels
- Hyatt Centric for a more standardized urban-lifestyle product

This category is often the most attractive for owners because a soft brand can preserve the hotel’s name, architecture and local identity while adding distribution and loyalty-system access. Accor reports that approximately half of its development projects are conversions, while Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt all actively position collection brands for independent properties. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/hotel-development/solutions-for-every-project?mdrv=group.accor.com&utm_source=openai))

### 3. Caribbean or coastal resort

For a traditional European-plan resort:

- Westin
- Marriott Hotels
- Autograph Collection
- Hilton Hotels & Resorts
- Curio Collection
- Hyatt Regency
- Destination by Hyatt
- MGallery
- Pullman
- Wyndham Grand
- Registry Collection

**Best resort shortlist:** Curio, Autograph, Destination by Hyatt, Westin, MGallery and Wyndham Grand/Registry.

The collection brands are particularly useful when the destination, architecture and resort experience are more important than rigid brand uniformity.

### 4. All-inclusive resort

Upper-upscale all-inclusive projects require a somewhat different operator universe. Consider:

- **Hyatt:** Hyatt Ziva, Hyatt Zilara and Dreams Resorts & Spas
- **Hilton:** Curio Collection or Hilton Hotels & Resorts all-inclusive
- **Marriott:** Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio or Marriott Hotels all-inclusive
- **IHG:** Iberostar Beachfront Resorts
- **Wyndham/Palladium:** Registry Collection, Grand Palladium and selected TRS structures
- **Meliá:** Meliá Hotels & Resorts and selected Paradisus projects
- **Barceló:** Barceló and selected Royal Level concepts
- **Accor:** Pullman or Mövenpick where available

Some of these are internally described as luxury rather than upper-upscale, but they may still be appropriate competitive-set candidates depending on room size, ADR, service intensity and food-and-beverage programming. Hyatt, for example, classifies Dreams and several of its other inclusive brands as “all-inclusive luxury.” ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai))

## Practical priority shortlist

If the owner wants to approach only the strongest initial candidates, I would recommend:

1. **Curio Collection by Hilton**
2. **Autograph Collection**
3. **Hyatt Regency**
4. **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt**
5. **Marriott Hotels or Westin**
6. **Hilton Hotels & Resorts**
7. **MGallery Collection**
8. **Pullman**
9. **Hotel Indigo**
10. **NH Collection**
11. **Wyndham Grand or Registry Collection**
12. **Renaissance or Hyatt Centric**

The final five-to-eight-brand RFP should be adjusted as follows:

- **Unique conversion:** Curio, Autograph, Unbound, MGallery, Hotel Indigo and Registry.
- **Large urban/MICE hotel:** Hyatt Regency, Marriott, Hilton, Westin, Pullman and Crowne Plaza.
- **Lifestyle city hotel:** Renaissance, Canopy, Hyatt Centric, JDV, Hotel Indigo and MGallery.
- **Beach resort:** Curio, Autograph, Destination by Hyatt, Westin, MGallery and Wyndham Grand.
- **All-inclusive:** Hyatt Inclusive Collection, Hilton/Curio, Marriott/Autograph, Iberostar, Registry/Palladium and Meliá.

## What the owner should compare in the RFP

Brand selection should ultimately be based on negotiated economics and expected contribution, including:

- Brand-reservation and loyalty contribution by feeder market
- Base, incentive, franchise, marketing and loyalty fees
- Required property-improvement plan and opening capital
- Brand-standard flexibility and waiver process
- Franchise versus management availability
- Owner termination and performance-test provisions
- Area-of-protection or noncompete terms
- Group, MICE and airline-crew sales capability
- All-inclusive revenue-management and procurement expertise
- Local technical-services and pre-opening resources
- Compatibility with residences, villas or mixed-use components
- Local-language support, payment systems, currency and tax structure

For most CALA projects, the strongest strategy is to compare **two conventional hard brands, three collection/lifestyle brands and one or two regional or all-inclusive specialists**, rather than assuming the largest global brand will necessarily produce the best owner return.
